item.description: BNP's elected members of parliament will not take oaths as members of the proposed Constitution Reform Council, as it is not recognised in the constitution, said BNP Standing Committee Member and MP Salahuddin Ahmed on Tuesday.Speaking at the oath-taking ceremony before the chief election commissioner's speech, Salahuddin said the decision was taken by the party."None of us have been elected as members of the Constitution Reform Council. item.description: If the newly-elected Members of Parliament from the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) do not take oath as members of the Constitution Reform Council, then members of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami will not take any oath, said the party’s Nayeb-e-Ameer Syed Abdullah Muhammad Taher to the media on Tuesday.Taher said that the oath ceremony for their newly-elected MPs has been scheduled for 12:00 PM. item.title: Trump says Cuba, a 'failed nation,' should make a deal with US

item.title: Pakistan Minister Ahsan Iqbal calls on CA
item.description: Pakistan's Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal Chaudhary paid a courtesy call on Chief Adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus at the State Guest House Jamuna on Tuesday, said the Chief Adviser's Press Wing.Chaudhary arrived here to attend the swearing-in ceremony of Bangladesh's new cabinet led by BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman, marking a significant diplomatic engagement between the two countries.

item.description: Members of Parliament from the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) have decided not to avail themselves of duty-free cars or government-allocated plots, said BNP media cell member Shairul Kabir Khan on Tuesday (17 February).The decision was taken at the inaugural meeting of the BNP parliamentary party held after the swearing-in ceremony earlier in the day.Shairul Kabir told reporters that none of the party’s MPs would accept the duty-free car facility.
